text:
Maria G.: quick heads-up — i'm planning to bump replicas on inference-statefulset from 2 -> 4 in eu-west1. change lives in infra/scale-inference branch. can someone do a config sanity check? mainly worried about pdb + rolling partition and preStop drain 

Kevin L.: tagging in. did you update the PVC/anti-affinity? also want to confirm readinessProbe timeouts don't cause premature kill during warmup. can you paste the tf diff or k8s snippet?

Maria G.: pasted the k8s bits below (from the helm values we render). it's basically replicas: 4, updateStrategy: RollingUpdate with partition control via our rollout controller. preStop added for connection drain.
```yaml
statefulset:
  replicas: 4
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - labelSelector:
                matchLabels:
                  app: inference
              topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
      containers:
        - name: runner
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 30"]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /live
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 6
```

Oliver R.: looks reasonable. two quick notes: 1) preStop sleep 30 is fine but if your app doesn't gracefully close connections within 30s we still lose inflight. consider SIGTERM handler that drains and only exits after pending requests drain. 2) for rollingUpdate on statefulset we usually control via the rollout controller by setting partition to current ordinal to pace the bump. don't set maxUnavailable — sts ignores it.

Tanvi S.: pdb question — current PDB for inference is minAvailable: 2. with replicas -> 4 i think minAvailable: 2 is okay for rolling but if you want stronger availability set to 3. what is acceptable outage? also HPA in this namespace: do we have an HPA that could fight the scale?

Maria G.: no HPA on inference-sts. our concern was PDB blocking eviction during node drains. we want cluster-admins to be able to cordon+drain one node without pdb blocking disruption. with replicas=4 and zone spread, minAvailable: 2 leaves room for one node drain.

Kevin L.: yeah minAvailable: 2 makes sense. for node drains we recommend PDB minAvailable = replicas - 2 so you can tolerate one node and one pod incidentally. if you want to guarantee zero capacity loss then minAvailable=4 but that prevents any eviction.

Oliver R.: small terraform nit: if you're changing replicas in tf template, also update the accompanying var docs and run a plan with --target=module.inference_statefulset.kubernetes_stateful_set.this to verify no other drift. sample plan excerpt: 
```
+ kubernetes_stateful_set.inference (module.inference_statefulset)
  # (changes: replicas: 2 -> 4)
```

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for branch infra/scale-inference — 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. (just a smoke run, see pipeline for full) :white_check_mark:

Tanvi S.: one more: readinessProbe.failureThreshold=6 + periodSeconds=5 gives ~30s retry window before restart. with initialDelaySeconds 5 total time = ~35s. ok? if warmup can be longer maybe bump initialDelaySeconds to 20.

Maria G.: good catch. i'll set initialDelaySeconds=20 and keep failureThreshold=6. i'll also set pdb minAvailable: 2 and add note for SIGTERM drain to the container entrypoint. i'll push the tf update in an hour and ping for a quick LGTM. thanks all :pray: 

Kevin L.: quick review offer — ping me when ready, will do a fast pass.

Oliver R.: i can test a staged partitioned rollout on dev cluster once you push. recommend partition=2 for first step so only ordinals >2 update.

Maria G.: perfect — will do partition=2 for the canary bump then full rollout after validation. i'll update PR description with test plan and expected metrics to watch (latency, pod restarts, attach errors).
